value.rationale: The exact infinite-family observation-cost law quantifies a nontrivial parity loss in two-frame sampling of spatially separated symbolic sensors. For even spacing four sensed coordinates can be tiled at optimal efficiency 1/4; for odd spacing a sharp local incidence obstruction forces a strictly greater observation density, with an explicit optimal schedule. This resolves a natural precise sampling-design invariant rather than an arbitrary small parameter case. The cost is explicitly metric/sensor-dependent, not claimed conjugacy invariant.
